extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS 2025 area chairs (ACs) / program committee members
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for serving as an Area Chair (AC) for NeurIPS 2025, covering responsibilities from bidding and conflict checking to leading discussions, ensuring review quality, writing meta-reviews, and coordinating with Senior Area Chairs (SACs) and Program Chairs (PCs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure papers have high-quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your job is to ensure that all the submissions you are assigned have high quality reviews and good discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read all reviews carefully. If a review is substandard, ask the reviewer to improve their review. Judge the quality of the review rather than relying on the reviewer's confidence score. You may need to send multiple reminder emails (be courteous). If a reviewer is unable to deliver, find a replacement reviewer. Do not dismiss or ignore a review unless you have a good reason for doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be familiar with technical content of assigned submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: You should become familiar with the technical contents of all your submissions and are responsible for making the initial acceptance decisions, with guidance from your senior area chair (SAC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be able to argue about technical content and contributions; if reviewers cannot agree, read the paper carefully and write a detailed meta-review. If overruling unanimous referees, the standards for your summary should be at the level of a full review and you should consider soliciting an auxiliary review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make initial accept/reject decisions with SAC guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: You are responsible for making the initial acceptance decisions, with guidance from your senior area chair (SAC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss borderline cases and any recommendations that go against reviewers with your SAC to help calibrate decisions across ACs. Best to take a decisive stand on borderline papers, using judgment where reviewers express neither excitement nor identify major problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid on papers honestly and promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Your bids are an important input to the paper matching process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bid in the specified window. Deceptive bidding practices will be investigated and may lead to removal from the PC and other penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check assignments and conflicts immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as you are notified of your assigned papers, you are expected to log in to OpenReview to check for conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments may change during the first week. Watch for notifications, and if you notice a conflict, contact your SAC immediately so the paper can be reassigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure timely completion of review-related tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the key dates (bidding, reviewing, emergency reviewing, author rebuttal, discussions, metareviews, SAC-AC/PC discussions, notifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect deadlines and respond to emails promptly. If you will be unavailable for more than a short period—especially during critical windows—notify your SAC as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate and lead discussions after author response
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as the author response is entered, initiate and lead a discussion via OpenReview for each submission and make sure the reviewers engage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and moderate the discussion to keep it respectful and steer it towards the most critical issues. You can restrict visibility of comments to appropriate readers (authors, reviewers, SAC, PCs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure reviewers read and respond to author responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure your reviewers read and respond to all author responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can initiate rolling discussions with authors after initial reviews and rebuttals. Ping reviewers to ensure engagement, especially during the one-week Reviewer-Author discussion phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage two-phase discussion process
rubrics_metrics.description: This year the discussion period is separated into two phases: Reviewer-Author Discussions and Reviewer-AC Discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 1 (Reviewer-Author): ask reviewers to read other reviews and author responses and engage with authors (one week). Phase 2 (Reviewer-AC): actively discuss the paper, reviews, and responses with reviewers; use this phase to prepare for metareview writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag and handle ethics concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure that any questionable papers are flagged for ethics review; these papers will be assigned ethics reviewers who effectively join the paper's assigned program committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you identify an ethics issue, flag it early so ethics reviewers can be assigned and consulted during the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite and manage emergency/additional reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: You may need to get additional/emergency reviewers in specified windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions for inviting emergency reviewers will be provided; organize emergency reviewing if assigned reviewers cannot complete their tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write clear, explanatory meta-reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a meta-review that explains your decision (accept, reject, borderline) to the authors; these are due by the metareview deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-review should augment the reviews and explain how reviews, author response, and discussion were used to arrive at the decision. Indicate that you read the author response (even a brief statement is fine). If you used information outside the reviews, disclose that to authors and state what it is. If reviewers disagree, write a detailed meta-review and consult your SAC if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not over-rely on numerical scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't focus too much on the scores. Instead, look carefully at the comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer confidence scores may reflect personality more than review quality. Base judgments primarily on substantive comments and evidence in reviews and discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be decisive on borderline and difficult cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Please attempt to take a decisive stand on borderline papers; these are often the toughest decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there is genuine disagreement, treat the case accordingly. If you want to overrule unanimous referees, prepare a summary at the level of a full review or solicit an auxiliary review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter biases and encourage risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to counter biases you perceive in the reviews; unfashionable subjects should be treated fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage risk and recognize that new approaches may not initially yield state-of-the-art results nor fit familiar presentation recipes. Avoid disadvantaging innovative or non-mainstream work due to bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: You must keep everything relating to the review process confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions in your own work until they are publicly available. Do not talk about or distribute submissions (code, ideas, results) to anyone without prior approval from program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid discussing assigned submissions with other ACs
rubrics_metrics.description: DO NOT talk to other ACs about submissions that are assigned to you; other ACs may have conflicts with these submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you feel it's important to discuss one submission in the context of another, email pc2025@neurips.cc. Your primary point of contact for discussions should be your SAC; your SAC does not have conflicts with your assigned submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not discuss your own submissions with SACs/ACs who have conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: DO NOT talk to other SACs or ACs about your own submissions or submissions with which you have a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow conflict-of-interest rules and avoid influencing review outcomes for submissions where you have a personal stake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report unethical or suspect behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: If you notice unethical or suspect behavior involving either authors or reviewers, notify your SAC and program chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt reporting ensures appropriate investigation and remedies; examples include deceptive bidding or other misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be professional and resist undue influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Be professional and listen to reviewers, but do not give in to undue influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your responsibility is to make good decisions, not just facilitate reviewer discussions. Be prepared to defend technical and editorial judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be kind and empathetic in communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibit empathy and understanding in all communications, acknowledging personal situations that may affect reviewers' work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer is unable to complete their work due to personal circumstances, be considerate—you might need to pick up the slack in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and maintain OpenReview/account setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that your preferred email address is accurate in your OpenReview profile and log into OpenReview with an up-to-date profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many emails are sent from noreply@openreview.net and can be marked as spam; check spam folders and whitelist the OpenReview email address to receive communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and abide by conference policies and checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and agree to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct, conflict of interest guidelines, and the paper checklist for authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also familiarize yourself with reviewer responsibilities, reviewer guidelines, and SAC guidelines as you will interact significantly with reviewers and SACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose and document use of external information
rubrics_metrics.description: If you use information not in the reviews (for example, from corresponding with a reviewer after the rebuttal), tell the authors that you have done so and explain what that information is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency is required when external communications inform decisions; include such disclosures in meta-reviews.
